01Dashboard SummaryOVERVIEW▶

Swami's entry in Izzy's design challenge: a replacement push key for a snow thrower, built to the SNOWTHROWERKEY master spec. Rather than one fixed model, this page is a parametric generator: every spec dimension is a live control, the 3D view updates as you type, and the part exports as STL, quad OBJ or a colour-coded 3MF, ready to slice in PETG. At the spec values it is one closed solid, 60.5 × 27.0 × 17.0 mm, that prints flat in one piece with no supports. The spec's benchmark log (timing plus every ambiguity and its workaround) is built in. Terms with a dotted underline jump to the Glossary.

Start hereOpen Key Generator to see and change the key, then export. To judge the entry, read Spec Issues & Workarounds and Benchmark Timeline.

03Thingiverse Model (Reference Only)SOURCE▶

Izzy mentioned an existing 3D model of this key on Thingiverse that prints in two pieces. Swami found what appears to be that model, Thingiverse thing 53277 ↗, and saved the composite image shown here. It is here for documentation only.

Not used for this modelNeither the Thingiverse model, its page nor this image was used in generating the Opus 5.5 key. By Swami's rule, the generator was built only from Izzy's spec and the photo of the original injection-moulded key; this section was added after the model was finished.
  • Two piecesThe Thingiverse key prints as two identical halves split at the mid-plane, so each half lies flat; this entry prints as one piece with a flat underside instead (see Design Approach).
  • HandleIts handle is a flat flared plate with a triangular pocket, like the OEM key; the spec here asks for a 17 mm thick glove grip with ribs and a lanyard hole.
  • StemIt shows a recessed stem with a square window near the tip, the same layout the spec describes.
04Key GeneratorGENERATOR▶

The live generator. Every dimension in the spec, plus the choices the spec left open, is a control on the right; the key rebuilds in about a quarter of a second and the 3D view, the mesh check and the Parameter Table follow along. The Export menu (STL, quad OBJ, a colour-coded 3MF, the parameter table, or everything in one zip) writes the part as it sits on the print bed (Z = 0), in millimetres, with the guard's stem-side face at X = 0.

Drag to orbit · right-drag to pan · scroll to zoom · click the view to use the hot keys shown on each button · hover a control for what it does · + marks a parameter this design added to the spec.

Defaults are the specOn first open the generator shows the spec values with Swami's rulings (33.5 mm stem, recess on both faces, single piece). Changes are remembered in this browser; reset all to spec in the Presets and reset group puts every value back, and the preset dropdown offers the OEM centred layout, deeper glove grooves and draft or fine mesh.
  • ViewsIso, top, bottom, front, back, left and right, perspective or orthographic, auto-spin and a full-window mode.
  • DisplaySolid, the quad mesh edges (what the OBJ holds), sharp feature edges, the print bed grid, axes and overall size labels.
  • Part coloursOpens colour coded: stem, guard, handle and grip & lanyard (rib grooves and the hole), the same colours as the matching control groups, the Parameter Table's Group tags and the 3MF export.
  • ColourFive PETG colours plus clear, a height map, and an overhang check that paints any downward face steeper than 45° from flat.
  • Section cutSlice along X, Y or Z with a slider; cut faces show orange, so the 1.3 mm web and the window are easy to inspect.
  • MeasureClick two points to read the distance and its X, Y and Z parts; the readout at top left shows the point under the cursor and which part it is on.

06Design ApproachDESIGN▶

How the key is built, part by part, and why. The model is one closed solid: 60.5 × 27.0 × 17.0 mm on the bed at the spec defaults, 7.24 cm³, 14,248 quads and 12 triangles.

  • DatumX = 0 is the guard's stem-side face, the spec's primary datum: the stem runs +X to 33.5 mm, the guard sits from −3 to 0 and the handle from −3 to −27. Y = 0 is the bilateral symmetry plane; Z is thickness, so the part prints flat.
  • MirrorThe spec asks for half-modelling and a Mirror. Here every grid line is generated for +Y and mirrored to −Y, so the left and right halves are identical to the last digit.
  • GridThe plan view is a boundary-fitted grid of stations (along X) and lanes (across Y). Lanes bend so that a grid line lands exactly on every edge: the stem outline, the notch, the recess rim, the window, the chamfer lines, the guard corners and the handle flare. Nothing is staircased.
  • ColumnsEach grid cell is a solid column from a bottom height to a top height. Tops and bottoms are quads; vertical walls are stitched wherever two neighbours differ, using every Z level met at that corner so no edge ends in the middle of another (no T-junctions). The result is a closed manifold, checked on every rebuild.
  • Lanyard holeAn O-grid: a square block of cells around the hole is warped so its inner rings lie on exact circles (the hole and its chamfer), blending back to the square grid outward.
  • SpeedThe whole build runs in the browser in about a quarter of a second, so every control is live.
PartFeatureHow it is modelled
StemBlade 9.5 × 4.1, 33.5 longRectangular columns from the guard face to the tip.
StemRecessed web, both facesFrom 1.4 mm in front of the guard to 1.4 mm before the window, inside a 1.4 mm rim, the columns drop to the 1.3 mm web. The block around the window and the tip stay solid for the latch.
StemLocking window 6 × 6Through cut at 22–28 mm with sharp edges (the latch bears on them).
StemSide notch, both sidesAn arc from 14 mm reaching 1.0 mm deep at 18 mm (radius 8.5 mm, tangent at the bottom), then a straight taper back to a point at 22 mm. The recess edge follows the notch so the rim stays 1.4 mm wide.
StemDiamond tip 5.5 × 2.6The last 5.5 mm tapers in plan from 9.5 mm to a 2.6 mm nose, an arrow point that self-centres in the switch barrel.
Stem0.5 mm chamfers45° chamfer on the top and bottom outline edges and the nose, plus the two nose corners in plan.
Guard3 × 18 × 11 collarIts 18 × 11 face has R2 corners; every face edge gets an R0.5 round to remove pinch points.
Handle12 → 27 mm flareA 5 mm straight neck, then a concave arc (radius 14.75 mm, solved) tangent to an R4 butt corner, reaching 27 mm at the butt.
Handle9.5 → 17 mm thicknessA smooth S-curve from 9.5 mm at the guard to 17 mm at 70% of the handle length, then level to the butt.
HandleRounded edgesR2.5 round on every handle edge, measured from the true outline so the flare and butt corners round evenly.
HandleGrip ribsRounded grooves 1.2 mm wide and 0.6 mm deep across both broad faces, 2.2 mm apart, fading out in the edge round and kept clear of the hole: 4 per face at the defaults.
HandleLanyard hole 4.5Through the handle centre (X = −15) with a 0.5 mm chamfer on both faces.
Why a flat undersideA key that is symmetric about its mid-plane cannot print flat in one piece: with a 17 mm handle and a 4.1 mm blade, the blade would hang 6.45 mm above the bed. That is why the Thingiverse model splits in two. This entry keeps one piece and drops every part's underside onto the bed, so the stem, guard and handle all print without supports. The guard then sits 3.45 mm higher than the stem's mid-plane, which the switch never sees. OEM centred in the generator restores the mid-plane layout for anyone printing with supports.
07Spec Issues & WorkaroundsBENCHMARK▶

The spec's benchmark protocol asks every entrant to log each ambiguity, conflict or gap and the workaround applied. These are the 22 found while building this entry, in the order met. Each Type tag is colour coded (conflict, ambiguity, missing detail, scope, note); the table is sortable.

#TypeFeatureSpec saysProblemWorkaround applied
01ConflictStem lengthstem_length: 34.0 mm, measured from the guard face to the tip.22.0 + 6.0 + 5.5 (window start + window + tip distance) is 33.5, not 34.0. The spec contradicts itself.Used 33.5 mm (Swami's ruling). stem_length is now derived from the three dimensions, so it can never disagree again.
02AmbiguityRecessstem_internal_thickness = stem_thickness - 2 x stem_edge_rim = 1.3 mm.The rim is a width, but the formula also uses it as a depth on both faces. Which faces carry the recess is not said.Recess on both faces (Swami's ruling), each 1.4 mm deep, leaving the 1.3 mm web. A control allows 0, 1 or 2 faces.
03AmbiguityRecessRecessed web width 6.7 mm (no length given).Where the recess starts and stops along the stem is not given, nor whether it surrounds the window.Recess runs from 1.4 mm in front of the guard to 1.4 mm before the window, inside the 1.4 mm rim. The window block and the tip stay solid so the latch bears on full 4.1 mm material, as on the OEM key in the photo.
04ConflictPrint layoutPrinted flat on bed; single piece; strict bilateral symmetry.A key symmetric about its mid-plane cannot print flat in one piece: with a 17 mm handle and a 4.1 mm blade, the blade would float 6.45 mm above the bed (the Thingiverse model splits in two for this reason).Default 'flat underside': every part's underside rests on Z = 0, so it prints in one piece with no supports. Left/right symmetry is kept. An 'OEM centred' switch restores the mid-plane layout.
05AmbiguityDiamond tipstem_tip_feature: diamond-shaped profile at the tip, 5.5 mm (length) x 2.6 mm (width).Not said whether the diamond is in plan, in side view, a raised emboss or the whole tip; 2.6 mm is narrower than the 4.1 mm thickness.The last 5.5 mm tapers in plan from 9.5 mm to a 2.6 mm flat nose (an arrow point) for self-centring. Taper length and nose width are parameters.
06AmbiguityDiamond tipstem_tip_distance 5.5 mm from the window to the tip; the diamond is also 5.5 mm long.The two 5.5 mm values coincide, so the taper starts exactly at the window's front edge, leaving no straight section in front of the window.Kept as written; the solid front bar is still 5.5 mm long and the window's side walls are 1.75 mm. A separate tip length control lets the taper start later.
07AmbiguitySide notch3-point arc cut at 14.0 mm, depth 1.0 mm, span 4.0 mm, tapering smoothly to a point over the subsequent 4.0 mm.Whether 14.0 mm is the start or the middle of the arc, which of the 3 points are meant, and whether one or both edges are cut are not given.14.0 mm is where the cut begins (same convention as stem_cutout_start). Arc from 14 to 18 mm reaching 1.0 mm deep, tangent at the bottom (R 8.5 mm), then a straight taper back to a point at 22 mm. Cut on both edges for symmetry.
08AmbiguitySide notchstem_edge_rim 1.4 mm solid perimeter wall.The 1.0 mm notch would leave only 0.4 mm of rim where it overlaps the recess.The recess edge follows the notch, so the rim stays a full 1.4 mm wide everywhere.
09AmbiguityChamferAll 90-degree leading edges and insertion corners feature a 0.5 mm chamfer.Which edges count as leading is not listed; chamfering the window would weaken the latch.0.5 mm 45-degree chamfer on all outer stem edges (top and bottom) and the nose, plus the nose corners in plan. Window edges left sharp. A switch limits it to the tip only.
10Missing detailGuardAll 4 external corners and edges are radiused/beveled.No radius or bevel size given; radius or bevel not chosen.R2.0 on the four corners of the 18 x 11 face and R0.5 on every face edge, both parameters.
11Missing detailGuardGuard is the primary datum; dimensions given as width x height.Its position relative to the stem and handle in Z is not stated.Centred on the stem in the OEM layout; bottom-aligned with the stem in the flat-underside layout. X = 0 is the guard's stem-side face.
12AmbiguityHandle outlinehandle_width 27.0 max, arcing down/tapering to 12.0 near the guard, with a 5.0 mm rounded edge transition zone before the arc begins.The arc radius, where the 27 mm is reached and what the 'rounded edge transition zone' is are not defined.A 5 mm straight neck at 12 mm, then a concave arc tangent to the neck and to an R4 butt corner, reaching 27 mm at the butt. The arc radius (14.75 mm) is solved from those constraints.
13Missing detailHandle thicknesshandle_height 17.0 mm max (thickness tapering down to 9.5 mm).The thickness profile along the handle is not given.Smooth S-curve from 9.5 mm at the guard to 17 mm at 70% of the handle length, then level to the butt. The peak position is a parameter.
14Missing detailHandle edgesErgonomics for heavy insulated winter gloves.No edge rounding is specified for the handle.R2.5 round on every handle edge, measured from the true outline so the flare and corners round evenly.
15Missing detailGrip ribsRidged/ribbed texture cut into the thickness faces.Count, size, spacing, direction and even which faces 'thickness faces' means are not given.Transverse rounded grooves (across the pull direction) on both broad faces: 1.2 mm wide, 0.6 mm deep, 2.2 mm pitch, faded out in the edge rounds. All four are parameters.
16ConflictLanyard holeThrough-hole centred in the handle body, 4.5 mm.Centred along the length puts the hole in the middle of the grip area, so ribs and hole compete for space.Hole at the handle's mid-length (X = -15 mm) with a 0.5 mm chamfer on both faces; ribs placed either side of it (4 per face). An offset control moves the hole.
17Missing detailHandle lengthhandle_length 24.0 mm.Not said where it is measured from.Measured from the guard's back face to the butt; overall key length 60.5 mm.
18ScopeDeliverableExport a native .f3d or .step file plus the parametric timeline.This entry is a browser-based mesh generator, not a CAD timeline.Per Swami: STL and quad OBJ now; a Fusion model may be a separate entry. The full parameter set exports as JSON and is listed in the Parameter Table.
19ScopeParametric CADEvery dimension in the F360 Parameter Table; fully constrained, locked sketches.Sketch constraints and a Fusion timeline do not exist in a mesh generator.Equivalent intent: every dimension is a named live parameter, derived values are computed, and the mesh is rebuilt deterministically from them on each change.
20Missing detailStem rootPure axial insertion and extraction against a spring-loaded barrel.No fillet is specified where the stem meets the guard, the most stressed spot when pulled by the lanyard.Left sharp to keep the full stem length usable in the barrel; flagged in the Print and Test Guide as the first place to check.
21ScopePhoto detailOriginal key photo shows a triangular pocket on the handle and a '32' moulding mark.Neither is in the spec.Not modelled; the spec's grip ribs take the pocket's place.
22NoteThin web4+ perimeters, 35-40% gyroid infill.The 1.3 mm web and 1.4 mm rims are thinner than 4 perimeters, so infill never reaches them.No change needed: those areas print as solid perimeters, which is stronger. Noted in the Print and Test Guide.

09Print & Test GuidePRINT▶
  • OrientationAs exported: broad face down, Z = 0 on the bed. With the default flat underside nothing needs support; run the overhang check colour mode to confirm after any change.
  • Walls4 or more perimeters, per the spec. At a 0.4 mm nozzle that makes the 1.4 mm stem rim and the 1.75 mm walls beside the window solid plastic.
  • Infill35–40% gyroid, per the spec; it only reaches the guard and the handle, since the stem is all perimeters.
  • Layers0.15–0.2 mm. The 1.3 mm web is about 7 layers at 0.2 mm; the recess floors bridge 6.7 mm, which PETG handles well with cooling at 30–50%.
  • TemperaturesTypical PETG: nozzle 230–245 °C, bed 70–85 °C. Use glue stick or a textured sheet; PETG sticks too hard to bare smooth PEI.
  • First layerTurn on elephant-foot compensation (about 0.15 mm) so the window and the blade width stay true.
  • GaugeMeasure the blade (9.5 × 4.1) and the window (6 × 6) with calipers before trying the switch.
  • InsertionPush straight in; the diamond nose should centre itself. If it binds, raise stem_chamfer or lower stem_width by 0.1 mm and reprint.
  • LatchThe switch's catch drops into the window; the solid block around the window carries that load.
  • Pull testClip the lanyard and pull along the axis; the stem-to-guard joint is the weakest point, so watch there first.

ExportsSTL is binary, with each quad split on its shorter diagonal. The OBJ keeps the quads (14,248 of them at the defaults, plus 12 triangles where a wall steps), which is what a subdivision or CAD tool wants. The 3MF is the same closed mesh with every triangle tagged by part: core 3MF base colours (stem green, guard yellow, handle orange, grip & lanyard pink) plus Bambu/Orca and PrusaSlicer paint data assigning filaments 1 to 4, so a multi-colour printer can print the colour coding (load four filaments, or set them all to one colour). All three are in millimetres with the part on Z = 0. Each one downloads as its own file. On claude.ai the save dialog accepts zip files rather than .stl, .obj or .3mf, so there each 3D export arrives inside a small .zip.

12GlossarySOURCE▶

Every term with a dotted underline in the dashboard links here — hover it for a quick definition, click it to land on its row. In the Appears in column, each number is a jump link to where that term is used in that section (hover to preview the line); the term flashes green when you arrive. Qty counts every mention of the term across the content sections (everything except the summary, this glossary and the references), including repeats within a section. Each term's Topic tag names what it is about, one color per topic.

TermTopicDefinitionAppears inQty
PETGMaterialsA tough, slightly flexible 3D printing plastic (glycol-modified PET); the spec's chosen material.
PerimeterPrintingAn outline wall the slicer prints around each layer; the spec asks for 4 or more.
Gyroid infillPrintingA wavy 3D infill pattern that is equally strong in every direction.
OverhangPrintingA downward-facing surface printed over air; steeper than about 45° from vertical it needs support.
BridgePrintingA span printed in mid-air between two supports, like the floor of the stem recess.
STLFilesThe standard triangle-mesh file for 3D printing; holds only surface triangles.
OBJFilesA mesh file that can hold quads and other polygons, not just triangles.
STEP / f3dFilesCAD exchange formats (solid boundary models); the spec asks for them, Swami chose meshes for now.
Quad meshMeshA mesh made mostly of four-sided faces; cleaner to edit than triangles.
Closed manifoldMeshA mesh with no holes in which every edge joins exactly two faces; slicers can fill it without repair.
T-junctionMeshA vertex sitting on the middle of another face's edge; it leaves hairline gaps in a mesh.
O-gridMeshA grid block bent into rings around a round hole so the hole edge is a true circle.
GenusMeshThe number of through-holes in a closed solid; this key has two.
Station / laneMeshStations are the grid lines across the key at set X positions; lanes run along it at set Y positions.
DatumDesignThe reference face every dimension is measured from; here the guard's stem-side face.
Bilateral symmetryDesignLeft and right halves are mirror images about the key's long axis.
ChamferDesignA flat 45° bevel cut on an edge; eases insertion and removes sharp corners.
Round / radiusDesignA curved edge or corner of a given radius (written R2 for a 2 mm radius).
StemKey partsThe flat insertion blade that goes into the snow thrower's switch barrel.
GuardKey partsThe stop flange between the stem and the handle; it stops the key at the right depth.
Web / rimKey partsThe thin recessed middle of the stem (1.3 mm) and the solid border around it (1.4 mm).
Locking windowKey partsThe 6 mm square hole the switch's spring catch drops into.
Side notchKey partsA shallow arc cut in both blade edges, 14 mm from the guard.
Lanyard holeKey partsThe 4.5 mm hole in the handle for the coiled tether to the dashboard.
Diamond tipKey partsThe tapered 5.5 mm nose of the stem, narrowing to 2.6 mm.
OrthographicViewerA view without perspective, so equal lengths look equal anywhere on screen.
Section cutViewerA plane that hides everything on one side so the inside can be seen.
FusionFilesAutodesk Fusion (formerly Fusion 360), the CAD program the spec was written for.

SNOWTHROWERKEY: Master Design Specification & Benchmark Protocol

  • Target Material: PETG (Printed flat on bed, 4+ perimeters, 35–40% gyroid infill)
  • Design Strategy & Intent:
    • Fully Parametric Architecture: Every dimension, offset, and feature must be fully driven by user parameters in the F360 Parameter Table so future changes can be made instantly without breaking the timeline or sketches.
    • Locked & Fully Constrained Sketches: All sketches must be fully constrained (locked) to prevent geometry drift, unlinked dimensions, or timeline failures during parameter updates.
    • Symmetry & Mirroring Workflow: The key exhibits strict bilateral symmetry along its central longitudinal axis. Recommended CAD construction is to model the primary profile/features relative to the central plane and utilize the Mirror feature to construct the full geometry, reducing timeline complexity and ensuring perfect symmetry.
    • Datum-Driven Alignment: Symmetrical master component (SNOWTHROWERKEY) utilizing the central Guard/Collar as the primary datum reference.
    • Mechanism Type: Pure linear push-in action (zero rotational torque; pure axial insertion and extraction forces against a spring-loaded switch barrel).
    • Ergonomics & Retention: Scaled for heavy insulated winter work gloves, featuring an integrated lanyard hole for spring-tether retention to the snow thrower dashboard.
    • Deliverable Requirement: Each participant must export a native CAD file (.f3d) or universal exchange file (.step) alongside the parametric timeline so the design can be immediately sliced in Orca/PrusaSlicer, printed in PETG, and physically tested for mechanical strength and switch accuracy.
    • Benchmark Evaluation Protocol: All participants (AIs and human engineers) must track and document:
      • Processing / Modeling Timeline: Total time required from prompt intake to final model generation.
      • Specification Errors & Workarounds: Explicit logging of any ambiguities, conflicting constraints, or missing details encountered in the spec, along with the engineering workaround applied.

1. STEM (Insertion Blade Component)

  • stem_length: 34.0 mm (Measured from the face of the guard to the tip)
  • stem_width: 9.5 mm
  • stem_thickness: 4.1 mm
  • stem_edge_rim: 1.4 mm (Width of the outer solid perimeter wall)
  • stem_internal_thickness: stem_thickness - (2 * stem_edge_rim) = 1.3 mm (Recessed web thickness)
  • stem_internal_width: stem_width - (2 * stem_edge_rim) = 6.7 mm (Recessed web width)
  • stem_cutout_start: 22.0 mm (Distance from guard face where the locking window begins)
  • stem_cutout_size: 6.0 mm square window
  • stem_tip_distance: 5.5 mm (Distance from the square cutout to the absolute tip)
  • stem_tip_feature: Diamond-shaped profile at the tip measuring 5.5 mm (length along axis) x 2.6 mm (width)
  • stem_side_notch: 3-point arc cut located at 14.0 mm from the guard, with a depth of 1.0 mm and a span width of 4.0 mm, tapering smoothly to a point over the subsequent 4.0 mm.
  • stem_chamfer: All 90-degree leading edges and insertion corners feature a 0.5 mm chamfer for smooth entry into the spring-loaded switch barrel.

2. GUARD (Collar / Stop Flange Component)

  • guard_length: 3.0 mm (Thickness along the longitudinal axis)
  • guard_width: 18.0 mm (Transverse span)
  • guard_height: 11.0 mm (Vertical span)
  • guard_edge_treatment: All 4 external corners and edges are radiused/beveled to eliminate sharp pinch points.

3. HANDLE (Grip & Ergonomics Component)

  • handle_length: 24.0 mm
  • handle_width: 27.0 mm max (arcing down/tapering to 12.0 mm near the guard, with a 5.0 mm rounded edge transition zone before the arc begins). Note: Scaled up slightly from original OEM to accommodate heavy insulated winter work gloves.
  • handle_height: 17.0 mm max (thickness tapering down to 9.5 mm).
  • handle_grip_texture: Ergonomic ridged/ribbed surface texture cut into the thickness faces to prevent slipping with wet gloves.
  • handle_lanyard_hole: Through-hole centered in the handle body (diameter: 4.5 mm) to allow attachment of a coiled spring tether/lanyard connecting it to the snow thrower dashboard.
